## Executive summary: Outlook totally reliant on China 



- At current prices mines are not cutting back. The onus for reducing cathode output has shifted to smelters and refineries, with the issue of excess supply and poor copper demand eclipsing those of concentrate availability. 

- Copper demand is expected to fall sharply this year outside of China (-18%) and fabricators are preparing extended summer shut downs. Chinese growth is forecast to be higher than previously expected (+10.4%) due to higher scrap replacement and restocking effects than previously anticipated.  Global consumption is forecast to fall by 10.1% in 2009. 

- Scrap availability fell sharply in Q4 2008 and Q1 2009, as weak economic activity cut scrap generation and low prices trimmed the flow of material to the market.  Higher prices in Q2 led to an improvement in availability, reducing cathode replacement for scrap at semi fabricators.

## Executive summary: Outlook totally reliant on China (continued) 



- Strategic government purchases (Chinese SRB and Korean PPS) have now abated.  In addition, Chinese cathode imports in H1 of 1.8Mt are expected to ease in H2, as the arbitrage window has closed. 

- Demand growth in China is expected to ease in H2 and remain poor elsewhere, so the market should move into surplus.  With most of this accumulating in the world outside of China and assumed to end up in exchange warehouses, LME prices are likely to come under pressure over the rest of 2009. 

- Restocking driven growth in H1 2010 should see the market move into deficit and prices rise back towards $5,000/t.  In H2 2010, prices wi

ll come off as production grows but demand is expected to slow as restocking growth ends, leading to rising surpluses and falling prices. 4 © 2009 CRU International Limited confidential ## Executive summary: Outlook totally reliant on China (continued) - In 2011 prices will start the year at a low ebb and a stock overhang will keep them from rising rapidly, despite a modest annual deficit. - We continue to see refined copper demand sustained in the medium term as the full impact of government stimulus packages is felt. - Production growth will also begin to recover in 2011, but the effects of another round of mine cutbacks and project delays from the lower prices in late 2010 and early 2011 mean this will not be sufficient to meet the growth in demand. - The market will move into deficit in 2012 and 2013 as above average demand growth will be met by modest growth in supply. As a result, the modest deficit of 2011 will grow in 2012 and 2013, leading to rising prices that should average $2.50/lb by 2013. 5 © 2009 CRU International Limited confidential ## Structure of presentation ### **Comparison with last Quarterly** 1.
